terms.gloss: an enclitic, a word that leans on the word before it
evidence: Prisc. p. 977 P. (Lewis & Short s.v. encliticus)
terms.comment: From Greek ἐγκλιτικός: -que, -ve, -ne (Traupman 246). Traupman’s pupil calls -que postpositīvum, placed after, as against praepositīvum, placed before (240); Lewis & Short gives praepositīvus from Diomedes and Priscian, and does not list postpositīvus.

phrases.english: It is postpositive; and so it is called an enclitic.

sources: Lewis & Short: encliticus · Lewis & Short: praepositivus
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency (printed page numbers): p. 240, p. 246.
